newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault plans cost cuts, rationalisation.
newsitem.headline: Renault plans cost cuts, rationalisation.

text.p: French car maker Renault said on Wednesday it planned to make about 20 billion francs in cost cuts by the year 2000.
Renault Commercial Director Philippe Gamba said the cuts were needed to make the company more effective.

"What we have to do inside the company to be more effective is cut down on costs. We have a big objective of 20 billion francs we have to cut in the next three years, before 2000," Gamba said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
"If we do that we will have the right product at the right price."
Gamba also said the company faced further rationalisation.
"We are not yet at the end of rationalisation. What we have said is that until 2000 we will not close down another factory," he said.
"Obviously what we have to do is be competitive and if the capacity is too high compared to the possibility of sales we will have to do something."
